topic: Why the doctor dilates your eyes and what to expect (blurry, light sensitive for a few hours, don't drive)

youtube.title: Why eye drops before an eye exam? 👁️ What to expect #Shorts
youtube.description:
Why does the eye doctor put drops in your eyes before the check-up?
கண் பரிசோதனைக்கு முன் ஏன் கண் சொட்டு போடுகிறார்கள்? என்ன எதிர்பார்க்கலாம்?

• Dilating drops widen the pupil so the retina and optic nerve can be seen clearly
• It can catch early diabetic eye changes, glaucoma and retinal tears, often before symptoms
• Afterwards near vision is blurry and light feels harsh for a few hours; that's normal
• Don't drive or ride home; bring someone with you
• Carry sunglasses and plan a light few hours after
• Eye pain, redness or blur lasting beyond the day? Call the eye specialist

gmb.text: Why do eye doctors sometimes put drops in your eyes before an exam? The drops widen the pupil, like opening a door wider, so the retina and optic nerve at the back of the eye can be seen clearly. A dilated exam can catch early signs of diabetic eye disease, glaucoma and retinal tears, often before you notice any problem. After the drops, near vision is blurry and bright light feels harsh for a few hours. This is normal. Don't drive or ride home: bring someone with you and carry sunglasses. If eye pain, redness or blurred vision lasts beyond the day, call the eye specialist. If you are over 40 or have diabetes, regular eye checks matter. Book an eye test on WhatsApp: 044 4356 9998
